analysis: Isoniazid is an antibiotic commonly used in the treatment of tuberculosis. It is well-documented in medical literature that isoniazid can lead to a deficiency in Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine). This occurs because isoniazid acts as a pyridoxine antagonist, which can increase the excretion of pyridoxine and interfere with its absorption. The deficiency of Vitamin B6 can lead to symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy, which is why patients on isoniazid are often supplemented with Vitamin B6 to prevent these adverse effects. The enhanced information aligns with the standard medical consensus that Vitamin B6 deficiency is the most likely to occur in patients taking isoniazid.
